reference.evidence: POD and source audit only; all runtime observations remain pending.

purpose: Finite DM5 comparison against every DM6 row in date.json. Status is a source/POD gate, never a test result.

status_vocabulary.supported: DM5 POD and/or source exposes the candidate syntax.
status_vocabulary.different: DM5 exposes a related syntax but differs in accepted layout, configuration gate, or meaning.
status_vocabulary.unsupported: No corresponding DM5 public facade or token is exposed; source takes its documented fallback path.
status_vocabulary.undocumented-partition: DM5 source accepts a candidate-shaped partition but POD does not make that partition a public promise.

render_comparison.meaning: DM5 UnixDate creates each listed field; week directives use the DM5 week routines.
DM5 has no %N field. Its generic unknown-directive branch emits N without percent.
All 18 exist. DM5 %C/%u compose with numeric %z whereas DM6 default composition uses %Z; DM5 %l treats both six-month endpoints as in-window, while DM6 uses an exclusive upper boundary.
DM5 assigns all four literal outputs and drops a trailing lone percent.
DM5 has no %<...> selector grammar; its one-character unknown-token fallback begins by emitting the less-than sign.

posix_comparison.meaning: DM5 contains neither Use_POSIX_Printf configuration nor a POSIX renderer branch; existing same-letter tokens retain DM5 default meanings, while %g/%V follow generic fallback.
The DM6 row says these POSIX meanings are unavailable. DM5 likewise supplies its legacy default meaning for %c/%x/%X/%E/%O/%+; it has no POSIX modifier grammar.

pattern_comparison.meaning: DM5 exports ParseDate, ParseDateString, and UnixDate but neither exports nor implements ParseDateFormat/parse_format. Therefore none of DM6's 52 explicit-pattern directives, regex capture behavior, or pattern validity rules belongs to the DM5 public facade.

grammar_comparison.dm5_candidate: DM5 ISO compact/dashed calendar, ordinal, and week forms
grammar_comparison.meaning: DM5 documents a smaller named list and source permits flexible dashes and one/two-digit dashed components. It does not have DM6's current-field omission productions as a documented family.

grammar_comparison.dm5_candidate: YYYYMM, YYYY, YY-MM, YY
grammar_comparison.meaning: DM5 documents these partial forms, but not the DM6 leading-hyphen current-context or truncated-week spellings.

grammar_comparison.dm5_candidate: MM/DD, MM/DD/YY, MM/DD/YYYY, YYYY M D
grammar_comparison.meaning: DM5 accepts the candidate family but normalizes flexible separators, including mixtures; DM6 requires a repeated separator. DM5 source also accepts a year-first numeric arrangement.

grammar_comparison.dm5_candidate: named month/day/year arrangements
grammar_comparison.meaning: DM5 accepts documented named arrangements with flexible/optional separators; it also accepts several word-order permutations through normalization, so it is not the DM6 finite separator contract.

grammar_comparison.dm5_candidate: joined named-month arrangements
grammar_comparison.meaning: DM5 documents its own joined layouts and source accepts the normalized candidate family; the fixed-width and ordering partition differs from DM6.

grammar_comparison.dm5_candidate: MMM YYYY and YYYY MMM
grammar_comparison.meaning: DM5 source accepts month-year directly and supplies day 1; it is not controlled by DM6 Format_MMMYYYY or its first/last endpoint option.

grammar_comparison.dm5_candidate: weekday of current week; next/last weekday
grammar_comparison.meaning: DM5 recognizes localized weekday and adjacent-weekday forms.

grammar_comparison.dm5_candidate: ordinal weekday/day within a named month
grammar_comparison.meaning: DM5 recognizes ordinal weekday-in-month and last-day-in-month forms; localized ordinal/month partitions require runtime characterization.

grammar_comparison.dm5_candidate: ordinal weekday in year and weekday of numbered week
grammar_comparison.meaning: DM5 supports ordinal weekday and numbered-week forms, but the DM6 standalone 'last weekday in YYYY' is not a DM5 documented production.

grammar_comparison.dm5_candidate: next/last week or month
grammar_comparison.meaning: DM5 documents and implements week/month; the DM6 next/previous year candidate is absent from the reviewed DM5 branches.

grammar_comparison.dm5_candidate: today/tomorrow/yesterday and their British week forms
grammar_comparison.meaning: DM5 supports the relative words and week variants. Holiday-name parsing is not documented or found in ParseDateString, so the DM6 holiday-name candidate is unsupported.

grammar_comparison.dm5_candidate: HH:MN, HH:MN:SS, optional fractional seconds, optional AM/PM
grammar_comparison.meaning: DM5 documents a narrower time grammar; source parses fractional seconds only after seconds and discards them. DM6 fractional-minute/hour and hyphen-truncated productions are not documented DM5 forms.

grammar_comparison.dm5_candidate: none
grammar_comparison.meaning: DM5 documentation requires a time to include hour and minute, except hour plus AM/PM; it does not expose DM6 HH or -MN truncated ISO forms.

grammar_comparison.dm5_candidate: hour/minute, optional seconds/fraction, optional meridiem
grammar_comparison.meaning: DM5 supports the documented colon forms and hour-plus-meridiem form; it does not document the DM6 fractional minute/hour alternatives or their separator variants.

grammar_comparison.dm5_candidate: localized noon/midnight and optional time introducer
grammar_comparison.meaning: DM5 replaces configured special-time words before ordinary time parsing.

grammar_comparison.dm5_candidate: DM5 ISO date-time list with optional T and flexible dashes
grammar_comparison.meaning: DM5 accepts combined ISO forms but has a distinct layout/ambiguity contract; it does not expose the DM6 complete/truncated composition table.

grammar_comparison.dm5_candidate: non-ISO date with documented time and relative-delta forms
grammar_comparison.meaning: DM5 parses time independently before date and supports its listed relative forms, including later/ago variants; its production set and connective tolerance differ from DM6.

grammar_comparison.dm5_candidate: epoch signed-seconds
grammar_comparison.meaning: DM5 explicitly recognizes positive and negative epoch seconds. A zone suffix is not a documented DM5 epoch production.

grammar_comparison.dm5_candidate: now plus localized relative-day words
grammar_comparison.meaning: DM5 recognizes now as a synonym within its special-date handling. Zone suffix attachment needs observation.

grammar_comparison.dm5_candidate: name/abbreviation and offset +HH, +HHMM, +HH:MM with optional parenthesized text
grammar_comparison.meaning: DM5 only documents these three numeric offset widths, not DM6 second-resolution offsets or the whitespace-abbreviation alternatives as a finite public production.

runtime_obligations: Probe each supported/different candidate in an isolated DM5 process with fixed reference time/language/timezone.
For every different row, probe the stated DM6 boundary and DM5-specific production before making a portable assertion.
Verify unknown-token fallback and unsupported facade absence by public callability checks, not source inspection alone.
